summary: Initial discovery with Cornerstone Bank to understand data residency and compliance needs across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment options. Key concerns: GDPR regional residency for EU customers, HIPAA-ish controls for health-adjacent data, strict logging/PII redaction rules for finance, KMS/HSM key management, audit log retention and access, and vendor attestations. Redwood AE/SE outlined hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs and proposed next steps: send security artifacts, schedule SE deep dive, run EU trial.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-07
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 mins
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE); Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE); Jon Ramos (Redwood CSM); Martin Lee (Cornerstone - Head Cloud Ops); Sonia Alvarez (Cornerstone - CISO); Derek Patel (Cornerstone - Lead ML Eng); Emily Rhodes (Cornerstone - Compliance)

Summary:
(automated) quick notes - discussion around data residency requirements for EU and US, comparisons between Hosted/Dedicated/Private, compliance artifacts, logging restrictions especially for transaction traces, next steps to share SOC2/ISO docs and schedule deep dive.

Transcript:
00:00:03 Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, really appreciate you making time. quick intros?
00:00:10 Martin Lee: Yeah Martin here, Head of Cloud Ops at Cornerstone. we're evaluating options for hosting some inference workloads that touch customer financial data.
00:00:17 Sonia Alvarez: Sonia, CISO. main concern is data residency and auditability, plus minimizing vendor access to raw logs.
00:00:23 Derek Patel: Derek, lead ML. we're most interested in latency and cost but can't compromise on PII handling.
00:00:30 Alex Chen: Great. Priya from our SE team will run through some of the technical tradeoffs later. Today's goal: understand your constraints around GDPR, HIPAA-like controls, logging, and whether a hosted or private deployment makes sense.
00:00:42 Priya Kapoor: Hi all. quick agenda: ask about current stack and flow, what data touches the models, retention and redaction needs, and we can map to Redwood Hosted / Dedicated / Private.

00:02:05 Martin Lee: To give context, we have production in AWS us-east-1 for most customers, but we need EU residency for EU customers and some APAC for a pilot.
00:02:18 Alex Chen: Understood. So two residency zones. For Hosted, we have region pins - EU and US - but our hosted offering is multitenant in control plane, data plane can be pinned to regions. For Dedicated and Private, you get stronger isolation.
00:02:45 Sonia Alvarez: When you say control plane, do you mean Redwood manages keys? We prefer customer-managed keys if possible.
00:02:50 Priya Kapoor: yes, we support KMS integrations; customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported for Dedicated and Private, and for Hosted we have BYOK options in some tiers.
00:03:08 Emily Rhodes: what's the difference then between Dedicated and Private for compliance?
00:03:15 Priya Kapoor: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools in our cloud with tenant isolation at the infra level and stronger network controls; Redwood still operates the control plane but can restrict human access and provide audit logs. Private means a VPC or on-prem where you manage the control plane, full customer-managed networking and no Redwood access unless explicitly configured.
00:03:36 Sonia Alvarez: we need SOC2 and ISO attestations up front. also need to know about audit log retention and who can access them.
00:03:45 Alex Chen: absolutely, we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs. Audit logs: for Hosted we provide audit logs but retention windows and access policies vary; Dedicated includes longer retention and finer RBAC; Private hands those to you.
00:04:10 Derek Patel: A couple technical constraints: our prompts will include account numbers and masked SSNs; we need assurance that logging won't store raw PII in an accessible log. can logs be scrubbed or redacted at ingestion?
00:04:27 Priya Kapoor: yes - we have log redaction pipelines and can do prefix/KV cache redaction for queries. In Private you can run custom redactors. For Hosted we can configure redaction rules but need to validate on a case-by-case basis.
00:04:50 Martin Lee: Another concern, GDPR: EU customer data must remain in EU. is there any metadata or telemetry that crosses regions?
00:04:58 Alex Chen: We strive to localize data plane; control plane metadata like billing might be global. For strict GDPR residency we recommend Dedicated pinned to EU or Private deployment in EU to avoid any metadata crossing boundaries. We'll document what metadata is sent where.
00:05:24 Sonia Alvarez: HIPAA — not our primary but some partners send health-adjacent info. need BAAs?
00:05:31 Alex Chen: We can discuss BAA; Private deployments make BAAs easier since you control PHI. Hosted can be done but usually requires contract addenda.
00:05:44 Priya Kapoor: also worth considering inference options: do you need streaming responses or batch? streaming has more ephemeral KV cache concerns but we can tokenize and avoid storing full utterances.
00:06:05 Derek Patel: Latency SLOs — we're sensitive. if we go Private on-prem we can hit our 50ms target; Dedicated in eu-central is likely OK but need per-model benchmarks.
00:06:19 Alex Chen: we can run perf benchmarks. Priya can spin up a test run in eu-central and share latency/cost numbers.
00:06:30 Priya Kapoor: noted. i'll prepare a perf plan.
00:07:02 Martin Lee: On logging restrictions — finance compliance team says transaction traces must be retained for 7 years but access restricted to auditors only. Can Redwood support fine-grained RBAC on logs?
00:07:15 Priya Kapoor: yes Dedicated supports RBAC on audit logs; Private you control. For Hosted we have role-based access but less granular. We also offer export of logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies so you can manage long-term retention.
00:07:38 Sonia Alvarez: about vendor access — can we require MFA and IP allowlists for any Redwood operator access?
00:07:46 Alex Chen: yes for Dedicated and Private we can configure allowlists and require MFA and justify emergency break-glass processes.
00:08:05 Derek Patel: What about model version pinning and rollout? we need reproducibility for compliance.
00:08:12 Priya Kapoor: model pinning and rollout policies are supported; we keep model hashes and can snapshot a model + config so you can reproduce outputs for audits.
00:08:27 Martin Lee: Any concerns with PCI? Some transactions could hit card-not-present flows.
00:08:33 Sonia Alvarez: PCI scoping: ideally the inference layer isn't in PCI scope; but we need to know if logs or outputs could bring us into scope.
00:08:42 Priya Kapoor: good question. log redaction and not persisting card PANs can keep you out of scope; we'll collaborate with your PCI team.
00:09:15 Alex Chen: quick note on costs: Dedicated has reserved commits and predictable throughput. Private on-prem has higher upfront integration but minimal per-token costs. Hosted is easiest to start but may have multi-tenant control plane considerations.
00:09:38 Martin Lee: timeline — we want to pilot in EU in 6-8 weeks, and a production decision in Q3.
00:09:45 Alex Chen: that sounds doable. we'll send security pack and propose dates for SE deep dive.
00:10:10 Priya Kapoor: can i ask about your current encryption at rest approach?
00:10:15 Martin Lee: we use AWS KMS with customer keys for DBs.
00:10:20 Priya Kapoor: good, we'll document KMS integration for Dedicated and Private. Hosted BYOK requires an attestation step but is supported on specific tiers.
00:11:00 Derek Patel: A practical question: during PII redaction if a prompt contains a customer name, will the model still use it to generate relevant output if it's redacted from logs?
00:11:12 Priya Kapoor: yes redaction for logs is separate from runtime. the model can operate on the raw prompt in-memory; redaction only impacts persistence and logs. for stricter needs you can pre-process to token-replace sensitive fields before sending.
00:11:40 Emily Rhodes: on auditability — our auditors want traceability for who queried what and when; is that available?
00:11:48 Alex Chen: yes we provide audit trails with user IDs and request IDs; for Private you can centralize them into your SIEM.
00:12:02 Martin Lee: any third-party subprocessors? where are your backups stored for Hosted?
00:12:10 Alex Chen: we'll share the subprocessors list. backups for hosted can be regionally stored; for strict customers we recommend Dedicated or Private.
00:12:35 Sonia Alvarez: I want to flag retention windows: logs must be immutable for at least 2 years for some regs; can you support WORM or long immutability?
00:12:44 Priya Kapoor: Dedicated + log export to S3 with object lock can meet WORM requirements. Private you control retention policies.
00:13:20 Derek Patel: are there limitations on model quantization or custom kernels in Private?
00:13:26 Priya Kapoor: Private gives you max flexibility; Dedicated supports a subset of quantization profiles we certify. some custom kernel work may require collaboration with our runtime team.
00:13:50 Alex Chen: i'd like to cover some common objections — if you worry about Redwood having any access to raw customer data in Hosted, Dedicated reduces that surface and Private eliminates it. tradeoff is integration overhead and cost.
00:14:05 Martin Lee: Cost is a factor but compliance is non-negotiable. We'll need a TCO model.
00:14:12 Alex Chen: understood. Priya will put together a ballpark TCO for Dedicated vs Private for your expected throughput.
00:14:25 Jon Ramos: also if you sign up for Dedicated we can include a more stringent NDA and operator access controls as part of the contract.
00:14:37 Sonia Alvarez: Regarding SSO - we use SAML 2.0, and require SCIM for provisioning.
00:14:45 Priya Kapoor: we support SAML and SCIM; for Private you can fully manage identity.
00:15:10 Martin Lee: Ok let's get into some specifics - Derek, i'll let you outline the data flow.
00:15:15 Derek Patel: sure. user events come into our API, we do enrichment, then some text fields go to the model for classification/scoring. we want to ensure that anything PII is either tokenized or not logged. the model outputs are stored in an analytics DB - how do we prevent cross-linking?
00:15:36 Priya Kapoor: recommend tokenization pre-ingest and using per-customer keys for any persistent store. also consider using ephemeral request IDs for traces, and store those with limited access.
00:15:58 Emily Rhodes: do you have references in banking? any customers with similar controls?
00:16:04 Alex Chen: yes we have a few financial customers; i'll include anonymized case study details in the follow-up.
00:16:25 Martin Lee: about legal — procurement will need liability limits and data residency clauses. can you support data processing agreements with EU-specific language?
00:16:34 Alex Chen: yes, we have standard DPA templates and can add region clauses for Dedicated/Private.
00:17:00 Sonia Alvarez: Another technical detail: can audit logs exclude prompt text but include metadata like request ID and user ID? that's ideal.
00:17:09 Priya Kapoor: yes that's configurable; we can pseudonymize or hash prompt text in logs.
00:17:30 Derek Patel: For the EU pilot, can you guarantee model weights or model variants stay in region when using Redwood-hosted models?
00:17:38 Alex Chen: for hosted models we replicate model artifacts to the region for inference; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated pinned to region or Private.
00:17:56 Priya Kapoor: also note that some telemetry for model telemetry is aggregated and could be global; we'll provide a telemetry map.
00:18:20 Martin Lee: Who would be the point person for technical integration?
00:18:25 Alex Chen: Priya will be your SE lead; i'll coordinate procurement and security docs.
00:18:40 Priya Kapoor: i'll follow up with a proposed architecture for Dedicated and a Private checklist.
00:19:05 Sonia Alvarez: For BAA and HIPAA — who at Redwood handles BAAs?
00:19:12 Alex Chen: our legal and security teams handle that; i'll introduce you to them in the next email thread.
00:19:35 Derek Patel: One more question about logs: are request/response payloads ever accessible in plaintext to Redwood ops during incident debug?
00:19:45 Priya Kapoor: only under strict access controls and we can implement masking; in Dedicated and Private we minimize ops access and provide audit trails for any access.
00:20:10 Martin Lee: Could you share a sample of the admin console role perms?
00:20:16 Alex Chen: yes we'll include screenshots and RBAC matrix.
00:20:40 Emily Rhodes: On retention and deletion - if a user requests deletion under GDPR, can you purge all traces including analytics traces?
00:20:50 Priya Kapoor: we support delete-by-user across logs and request stores for Dedicated and Private; Hosted supports deletion but may require some extra steps for backups -- we'll document.
00:21:30 Martin Lee: ok timeline and next steps recap?
00:21:35 Alex Chen: recap: we'll send security pack (SOC2, ISO, subprocessors), Priya to propose SE deep dive week of May 19, Priya to run EU perf test, Cornerstone to share list of region requirements and sensitive datasets.
00:22:05 Sonia Alvarez: sounds good. any open blockers?
00:22:10 Derek Patel: none from tech side. need cost estimate though.
00:22:20 Alex Chen: we'll include TCO roughs.
00:22:40 Jon Ramos: i'll set the follow-up invite after we confirm SE availability.
00:23:00 Martin Lee: thanks everyone.
00:23:05 Alex Chen: thanks all.

(There is a short technical Q&A section between 00:30:00 and 00:45:00 that contains some live debugging chatter and vendor doc references, transcription slightly garbled)

00:30:02 Priya Kapoor: referencing the private deployment checklist link: [link to private-checklist.md]
00:31:10 Derek Patel: can you confirm the S3 export format for logs?
00:31:20 Priya Kapoor: JSON lines with metadata keys, and optionally obfuscated prompt_text.
00:33:40 Martin Lee: ok that's helpful.
00:40:02 Alex Chen: quick final notes - we'll make sure the follow-up includes a clear comparison matrix for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private with compliance implications.
00:41:12 Sonia Alvarez: please include a section on allowed operator actions and emergency access procedures.
00:41:30 Alex Chen: will do.
00:45:00 Meeting end.
